tagline: Why star schema outperforms flat denormalized tables in Power BI

slides.title: Star Schema vs Flat Table
slides.body: A star schema splits a denormalized flat table into one fact table (measures + foreign keys) and multiple dimension tables (descriptors). Each dimension connects to the fact via a single integer key.
slides.keyPoint: Star schema improves VertiPaq compression, query speed, DAX simplicity, and allows dimensions to serve multiple fact tables.

slides.title: Flat Table — All Data in One Table (Bad)
slides.caption: Customer name and product details repeat on every order row
slides.note: Alice's city 'London' appears twice — if she moves, you must update EVERY order row

slides.title: Fact Table — FactOrders
slides.note: Fact table keeps only integer keys and numeric measures — smallest possible row size for VertiPaq compression

slides.title: Dimension Tables — Each Descriptor Stored Once
slides.caption: Each dimension connects to FactOrders via its key column
rows: Date, Month, Quarter, Year, IsWeekend, FiscalYear
slides.note: Alice's city is stored once in DimCustomer — updating it there instantly updates all her orders

slides.title: Why Star Schema Wins in Power BI
bullets: Compression — integer keys compress far better than repeated text strings; smaller model = faster queries
Query speed — VertiPaq engine is optimized for single-direction (one-to-many) join traversal
Simpler DAX — RELATED() easily brings dimension attributes into measures without complex lookups
Reusable dimensions — DimDate can serve FactSales, FactBudget, FactForecast simultaneously
Update safety — changing a dimension attribute updates all related fact rows via the relationship
slides.keyPoint: PL-300 exam rule: star schema is almost always the correct answer when asked how to reduce model size, improve query performance, or fix a modeling design issue.
